newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian president leaves on regional tour.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian president leaves on regional tour.

text.p: Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov left on Wednesday for a five-day trip to Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary, the most economically advanced of the former East Bloc states.

Deputy Foreign Minister Boiko Mirchev told a news conference the visit would give Stoyanov the opportunity to reaffirm Bulgaria's desire to join the European Union, NATO, and the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA).
Stoyanov took office on January 22, inheriting a severe economic and political crisis. Bulgaria has fallen far behind other East European states considered its economic equals in the early 1990s.
"Bulgaria's most urgent task is to set the base for vital economic reforms, but at the same time it should clearly state its political goals and foreign policy priorities," Mirchev said.

"This is why President Stoyanov is going to visit these particular states -- to show the world what the country's ambitions and demands are, and with which countries it would like to be compared and amicably compete with," he said.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are among the front runners to join the European Union and NATO.
Last week, Bulgaria's caretaker government adopted a declaration expressing a desire for full NATO membership, an issue on which the former Socialist cabinet was ambiguous.

The document, strongly endorsed by Stoyanov, is intended to qualify the Balkan country of 8.4 million people for membership nomination at a NATO summit in July, when the pact will decide which new members to admit.
Stoyanov's first trip abroad after taking office was to Brussels in January, to drum up western European support for reforms planned to bring Bulgaria out of crisis.
After 30 days of mass protests fuelled by economic hardship, Stoyanov brokered an agreement between Bulgaria's political parties on February 4 for early general elections on April 19.

Mirchev said Stoyanov would try to prepare the ground for free trade agreements with Poland and Hungary, which are one condition for admission to CEFTA. Bulgaria already has a similar agreement with the Czech Republic.
Stoyanov will visit Poland on February 26 and 27, then the Czech Republic on February 28-March 1 and Hungary on March 1-2.
